statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about twenty-nine and a half hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; twenty of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress is 58 in the elevated band, one point higher than the previous hour, reflecting a weekend in which the shut Saudi East-West pipeline, Houthi control of Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb approaches, WTI at $100.05 and an August CPI print of 0.4 per cent remain unpriced ahead of Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart and a 16 September FOMC decision priced near 85.5 per cent for a 25 basis point hike. Confidence is 87: every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only missing evidence class is a live price path that no venue can supply while the market is closed.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in twenty of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures failed mean reversion has no path to measure for most of this horizon. Second, the last observed session was orderly and two-way rather than one-way: the cash range spanned only 159.61 points, the close finished about 105 points below the high, advancers led decliners by roughly 2.1 to 1, nine of eleven sectors rose and VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84. Third, none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail is observed, because observing them requires a live tape. The severity of the macro and geopolitical backdrop is therefore expressed in Stress at 58 rather than in Tail, consistent with the documented separation between a difficult environment and a pathological price path. The one narrow window flagged in this horizon is the 22:00 UTC restart and the two hours that follow it, where conditional Tail reaches the WATCH band on gap and thin-liquidity risk that is anticipated rather than observed.
headline: Nearly thirty hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the shut Saudi East-West pipeline keeps 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supply off its route, Houthi forces hold Perim island and the Bab el-Mandeb approaches, WTI sits at $100.05 after a 20 per cent month and a hot August CPI has left the 16 September FOMC priced near 85.5 per cent for a rate hike, leaving an unpriced weekend to meet Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. Breadth on the day was genuinely broad, with advancers ahead of decliners by about 2.1 to 1 and nine of eleven sectors higher. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against the macro backdrop. Delayed latest-session cross-asset context is consistent with that tape rather than with a risk-off cascade: index futures were higher across NQ, ES and YM, the volatility future fell more than eight per cent, gold was flat, Treasury futures were only marginally lower, seven of eight tracked megacaps rose and semiconductor leadership was broad. That context is delayed and is not evidence of a live price path.

The backdrop behind Stress is genuinely severe and pulls the other way. Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline on Friday after a drone strike that Riyadh and Baghdad both traced to Iraq; the line had been carrying 4 to 5 million barrels a day, 4 to 5 per cent of global supply, as the main route out for Middle East crude while the Strait of Hormuz stayed disrupted. Houthi forces seized Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb on Friday after taking Mocha and advancing on Dhubab, and have declared navigation safe for all shipping except Saudi vessels. The IEA reported Saudi crude supply at its lowest in more than three decades. WTI settled at $100.05 and Brent at $104.61, down 2.37 and 2.81 per cent on the day after Iranian state media flagged talks with Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, but still up about 9.7 per cent on the week and 20.15 per cent on the month, with U.S. diesel reported past a record $6 a gallon. Over the weekend Yemen's defence ministry reported counterattacks on Houthi targets, the United States is assisting Saudi forces with target coordination inside Yemen, and the Crown Prince has pressed for direct U.S. military action, which Washington has so far declined in favour of intelligence support. That mix of broadening conflict against a partial shipping carve-out and an active de-escalation track is why Stress moves one point to 58 rather than stepping sharply.

The rate channel is the second Stress input. August CPI, released Friday, rose 0.4 per cent on the month against 0.1 per cent in July and 3.4 per cent over twelve months, while core rose 0.3 per cent on the month, a tenth above forecast, and 2.4 per cent over the year. The energy index rose 2.1 per cent on the month and 16.3 per cent on the year, with gasoline up 3.9 per cent on the month and 27.4 per cent on the year, which is the channel through which the supply shock reaches the policy decision. Yields are correspondingly elevated: the 10 September H.15 observation shows the 2-year at 4.56 per cent, the 10-year at 4.95 per cent and the 30-year at 5.37 per cent against a federal funds effective rate of 3.63 per cent. The FOMC meets on 15 and 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections, and futures price roughly 85.5 per cent odds of a 25 basis point increase to 3.75 to 4.00 per cent on Wednesday.

Tail nevertheless stays at 6. The documented separation is deliberate: event importance, surprise magnitude, forecast dispersion and generic volatility belong in Stress and Confidence, while Tail requires an observed price path that denies meaningful retracement. For most of this horizon no such path can exist, and the last one that did exist was orderly. The single narrow window worth flagging is the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, where an entire weekend of pipeline, Perim, counteroffensive and inflation news meets a book that has not quoted since Friday evening. Conditional Tail reaches 22 there and eases to 21 and 20 across the following two hours, which maps to WATCH and defines the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. That step is anticipatory and is held inside the WATCH band rather than pushed to a blocking level, because a hypothetical gap is not an observed one and a restart that reprices in an orderly two-way fashion would justify a prompt return to the low band.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 02:00 UTC on 12 September to 01:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there for the rest of the window, in normal mode throughout, tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 59 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53 and 56 to 57 by the close of the window as attention turned to the restart and the weekend escalation reports. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 in the middle of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window is a revision: each slot reproduces the value published at that hour.
outlookSummary: Twenty of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's twenty-first slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It steps to 22 in the restart hour, then eases to 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, and returns to 19 by 01:00 UTC on Monday. Those three WATCH slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. Stress rises from 58 through a 64 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture and the approaching FOMC, then eases to 60 as Asian pricing establishes. Confidence declines gently from 87 to 78 at the restart, reflecting the widening gap between the last verified print and the hour being described, before recovering to 80 once a live venue exists again. Every slot after the first frames structure conditionally: no gap direction, pullback depth or retracement behaviour is claimed as observed, and the 16 September FOMC decision with its Summary of Economic Projections sits beyond this horizon.
